claims.text: The document prints McCandlish's testimony under the date 'December 2000', in section 3.8.5 'Technology / Science', with an editorial preface that states its own summary of what the reader will learn, including 'In addition, we have the drawing from aerospace inventor Brad Sorenson of the devices that he saw, as well as a schematic of one of these alien reproduction vehicles - in some remarkable detail.'

The same document carries a separate 'Testimony of Lieutenant Colonel John Williams / September 2000' which states of Norton AFB: 'I was never allowed in that area when I was there at Norton Air Force Base', and, asked how he could validate the facility existed, 'That's correct because I was responsible for that base's facilities from 1981-82.'

The compiler cross-references his own two witnesses to each other in bracketed editorial notes signed 'SG', including '[See the testimony of Mark McCandlish which establishes that indeed a UFO was stored at this facility at Norton AFB. SG]'. The corroboration between the two testimonies is asserted by the compiler, inside the compilation.
The document is the origin in print of the craft's two names: 'Well, this craft was what they called the Alien Reproduction Vehicle; it was also nicknamed the Flux Liner.'

desc: The Briefing Document is the custody point for dozens of this board's witness claims, not only this one, and it is openable in full as OCR text on archive.org. It prints McCandlish's testimony at section 3.8.5 under the date December 2000, and it is where the claimed craft acquires its two names in print. It also prints, separately, the September 2000 testimony of Lt Col John Williams on a compartmented facility at Norton AFB, and its compiler cross-references the two witnesses to each other in bracketed editorial notes signed 'SG'. That is the document's characteristic move and the reason its claims about the world cap at Tier 2: the corroboration between the two testimonies is asserted by the compiler, inside the compilation. Its claims about its own contents are another matter and are documented, because the contents can be read.
